title: How do I make sponsor deliverables without rebuilding the whole episode?
summary: Create sponsor-specific video deliverables from an existing episode while preserving the main story, approved wording, and clear version ownership.
body_markdown:
## What you’ll take away


- Separate a sponsor's requested asset from changes to the main episode.
- Use the actual approved source statement rather than implying a new endorsement.
- Keep version names and requested changes clear across reviews.


## Separate the two jobs in the sponsor request


A request for a standalone clip is different from a correction inside the full episode. List which changes affect the main program and which apply only to the sponsor asset. Do not let a separate promotional deliverable quietly become the new master episode.


For an illustrative request, the sponsor wants the host's product explanation as a short clip and a corrected product name in the next episode revision. The clip needs its own opening context; the correction needs the appropriate recorded wording or an approved pickup. They should not be handled as one vague instruction to “make the sponsor version.”


## Confirm the actual statement and intended use


Locate the recorded sponsor passage and its surrounding context. If the new asset would make a recommendation appear broader than the original statement, revise the brief. A short excerpt still needs to represent what the speaker meant.


Use the approved wording and your established sponsorship review requirements. If a new sentence is needed, record or obtain it through the appropriate process. Do not ask an assistant to manufacture an endorsement in the host's voice simply to avoid a pickup.


## Create a separate editable sequence


In Wideframe, identify a copy of the current episode project and the specific source passage. The[review-note recipe](https://try.wideframe.com/skills/apply-review-notes/) supports explicit changes as a new version. Add the recipe in a new chat if useful, then name the output according to its actual purpose.


Keep the main episode and sponsor clip clearly distinguished. If the full episode needs a factual correction too, create that revision separately. A clear version structure prevents a short promotional export from becoming the accidental source for the next long-form edit.


## Make the standalone clip understandable


An episode mention may begin with a reference to a previous conversation or a transition from the show's content. Give the standalone clip enough identity and context to work outside the episode. Remove unrelated lead-in only when the remaining statement stays coherent.


Use product footage where it clarifies the host's explanation. Keep any relevant qualification in the source and captions. Do not add a headline that turns a personal experience into a universal performance claim. The sponsor's desired message must still fit the actual material.


## Protect the main story from unnecessary changes


If the requested asset is separate, the main episode may need no structural change. Keep its pacing and narrative intact. When an in-episode correction is required, check the transition into and out of the sponsor passage so the replacement does not disrupt the program.


A shorter sponsor passage may leave an awkward musical or visual transition. Resolve that in the episode version rather than assuming a text change is the only affected element. The editor's finishing pass should consider the whole section.


## Deliver the right version with clear notes


Name the files so the sponsor and producer know whether they are reviewing the standalone clip or the episode revision. Include a short description of what changed. Keep review comments attached to the correct output.


Use explicit timecoded notes for subsequent edits, and resolve subjective requests before delegating them. If a sponsor asks for a new claim, treat that as new content requiring an appropriate source and approval, not merely a caption replacement.


## Keep reusable pieces without making them stale


Save the source passage, approved product assets, and the sequence relationships for later revisions. Update sponsor details when a new campaign changes wording, links, or allowed use. Do not assume last month's instructions apply indefinitely.


The recurring assistant task is preparing and revising a clearly scoped asset from an existing project. The main episode remains a coherent editorial work, while sponsor deliverables can evolve without rebuilding it from the beginning.
